name: South America: Chile

outcome.intro: After studying this section, a student will learn where Chilean wine regions are located, understand the unique climate, and recognize the primary grape varieties planted.
outcome.certified: After studying this section, a candidate will learn the major geographical influences that affect vine growing, how the major grape varieties grown in Chile arrived in the country, have a familiarity with the Denominación de Origen (DO) system, and recognize major growing areas and major subregions. A Certified Sommelier will be able to recognize iconic producers and be able to recommend and sell food pairings with wines from Chile to a guest.

rows.intro: Located on the west coast of South America in the Southern Hemisphere.; 2,670 miles or 4300 km north to south.; 217 miles or 350 km wide.; Spans 17-53°S latitude.
Hot desert to cool to cold from north to south.
Desert: Atacama Desert; Ocean: Pacific Ocean, provides cool breezes and fog.; Mountains:; Andes Mountains: Elevation and diurnal shifts.; Coastal Range: Creates rain shadow from cold Pacific.
No presence of phylloxera (because of sandy soil).; Irrigation is essential from the Andes.; Mostly ungrafted vines.
Denominación de Origen (DO) System:; Refers to a geographic place of origin only, no other additional laws.; Region, Subregion, Zone, Area.
rows.certified: Minimum Percentages:; Variety/Vintage/Origin Labeling is 75%.; In practice, EU requires 85% in all three categories.

rows.intro: Aconcagua DO; Subregion: Casablanca DO; Cool, maritime climate west of the Coastal Range.; Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Noir; Valle Central DO; Warm to hot climate.; Located between the Coastal Range and Andes.; 80% of Chilean production.; Cabernet Sauvignon, Carménère, Merlot; Subregion: Valle de Maipo DO; Surrounds Santiago in the Maipo River Valley.; Most of the major historical wineries are located here.; Cabernet Sauvignon
rows.certified: All Regions; Aconcagua DO; Casablanca DO; Valle Central DO; Rapel DO; Colchagua DO; Cachapoal DO; Curicó Valley DO; Maule DO; Valle de Maipo DO

rows.intro: Humboldt Current:; Cold current coming from Antarctica running along the west coast of South America.
Often big, intense, fruit driven, high-alcohol wines.

rows.certified: Concha y Toro, Santa Rita, Errázuriz, Casa Lapostolle, Carmen

rows.intro: 1500s: Grapes being grown in the South American Spanish colonies.; 1600s: Prohibitive laws from the Spanish restricting wine production.; 1800s: Political independence and influx of European immigrants led to an expansion of viticulture.; 1970s-80s: Influx of foreign investment.
